title: Build a metric identity that stays bounded
description: Choose dimensions and a publication interval. The model multiplies possible dimension values into distinct time series and shows the resulting daily data-point volume.

dimensions.label: Service
dimensions.detail: A small, owned service catalog supports service-level diagnosis.

dimensions.label: Environment
dimensions.detail: A fixed deployment environment separates production from test traffic.

dimensions.label: Region
dimensions.detail: A bounded Region set reveals location-specific failures.

dimensions.label: Operation
dimensions.detail: A controlled operation name can isolate a failing code path.

dimensions.label: Status class
dimensions.detail: A small class is usually safer than every raw status or error string.

dimensions.label: Instance ID
dimensions.detail: Resource identity can help diagnosis, but churn expands the active series set.

dimensions.label: Request ID
dimensions.detail: Put request identity in logs or traces. As a metric dimension it creates a series per request.

publicationIntervals.label: 1 second
publicationIntervals.detail: High-resolution signal for a proven sub-minute response need.

publicationIntervals.label: 10 seconds
publicationIntervals.detail: Fast feedback with one tenth of the one-second publication volume.

publicationIntervals.label: 1 minute
publicationIntervals.detail: A common starting point for service health metrics.

publicationIntervals.label: 5 minutes
publicationIntervals.detail: Lower-volume signal for slower operational decisions.

reviewBands.note: These are lesson review bands, not CloudWatch service quotas or pricing tiers.
